stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\in\{1,\dots,K\}</annotation></semantics></math>, which are subsequently mapped to continuous local plans <math id="S4.SS3.SSS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\bm{\tau}_{t}^{(k)}\}_{k=1}^{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>𝝉</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\bm{\tau}_{t}^{(k)}\}_{k=1}^{K}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection"><span id="S4.SS3.SSS2.6" class="ltx_text">IV-C</span>2 </span>Temporal Consistency</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Receding-horizon planning under partial observability is often inherently multi-modal, where valid paths exist in distinct topological modes <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>]</cite> (<span id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">e.g.,</span> bypassing an obstacle from left or right). If consecutive plans switch between these modes, the executed behavior may oscillate, yielding jittery headings and collisions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>]</cite>.
To increase temporal consistency in the generated candidates, we augment the conditioning signal with an explicit previous-plan token <math id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{t}^{\mathrm{prev}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>prev</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{t}^{\mathrm{prev}}</annotation></semantics></math> representing the heading direction from the previously selected trajectory <math id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\tau}_{t-1}^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝝉</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\tau}_{t-1}^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">With a clamped cubic B-spline, the initial heading direction is proportional to the difference between first and second control points, i.e., <math id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\dot{\tau}}(0)\propto(\mathbf{Q}_{t-1,1}-\mathbf{Q}_{t-1,0})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝝉</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∝</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐐</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐐</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\dot{\tau}}(0)\propto(\mathbf{Q}_{t-1,1}-\mathbf{Q}_{t-1,0})</annotation></semantics></math>.
In our robot-centric frame, the first control point is anchored at the origin <math id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{Q}_{t-1,0}=\mathbf{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐐</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>𝟎</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{Q}_{t-1,0}=\mathbf{0}</annotation></semantics></math>. The last heading direction is obtained as
<math id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{t}^{\mathrm{prev}}=\mathrm{norm}(\mathbf{Q}_{t-1,1}^{\star})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>prev</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>norm</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐐</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{t}^{\mathrm{prev}}=\mathrm{norm}(\mathbf{Q}_{t-1,1}^{\star})</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{Q}_{t-1,1}^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐐</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{Q}_{t-1,1}^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the second control point of <math id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{{\tau}_{t-1}}^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mmultiscripts><mi>𝝉</mi><mrow><mi>𝒕</mi><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">−</mo><mn>𝟏</mn></mrow><mrow></mrow><mrow></mrow><mo>⋆</mo></mmultiscripts><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{{\tau}_{t-1}}^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>. To simplify training and stabilize the learning process, we use privileged information for <math id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{t}^{\mathrm{prev}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>prev</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{t}^{\mathrm{prev}}</annotation></semantics></math>. During training process, <math id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{t}^{\mathrm{prev}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>prev</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{t}^{\mathrm{prev}}</annotation></semantics></math> is computed from the ground-truth expert control points <math id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\mathcal{\mathbf{Q}}}_{t,2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐐</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\mathcal{\mathbf{Q}}}_{t,2}</annotation></semantics></math> rather than from the previous step. For the first planning step, we use a learned null token to indicate the absence of previous-plan information.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S4.SS4.6" class="ltx_text">IV-D</span> </span><span id="S4.SS4.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Safety-Aware Candidate Selection via the Critic Module</span></h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While the diffusion policy effectively captures the multi-modal distribution of expert behaviors, the sampled trajectories are not guaranteed to satisfy safety constraints <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>, <a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">47</a>]</cite>. To decouple complex distribution modeling from strict safety verification, we employ a generate-and-select pipeline. At each planning <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, the diffusion policy samples <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> candidate control-point sets <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathcal{Q}^{(k)}_{t}\}_{k=1}^{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒬</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathcal{Q}^{(k)}_{t}\}_{k=1}^{K}</annotation></semantics></math> conditioned on the context <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\mathcal{C}}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝓒</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\mathcal{C}}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, which generate continuous trajectories <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\bm{\tau_{t}}^{(k)}\}_{k=1}^{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>𝝉</mi><mi>𝒕</mi><mrow></mrow><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mmultiscripts><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\bm{\tau_{t}}^{(k)}\}_{k=1}^{K}</annotation></semantics></math>. These are evaluated by an explicit geometric critic, which selects the optimal one <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{{\tau}_{t}^{\star}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝝉</mi><mi>𝒕</mi><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">⋆</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{{\tau}_{t}^{\star}}</annotation></semantics></math> by minimizing a cost function <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>J</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\tau}_{t}^{\star}\;=\;\underset{\bm{\tau}\in\{\bm{\tau}^{(k)}_{t}\}_{k=1}^{K}}{\arg\min}\;J\!\left(\bm{\tau}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝝉</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>min</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathsize="0.700em">𝝉</mi><mo mathsize="0.700em">∈</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi mathsize="0.700em">𝝉</mi><mi mathsize="0.710em">t</mi><mrow><mo maxsize="0.710em" minsize="0.710em">(</mo><mi mathsize="0.710em">k</mi><mo maxsize="0.710em" minsize="0.710em">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi mathsize="0.710em">k</mi><mo mathsize="0.710em">=</mo><mn mathsize="0.710em">1</mn></mrow><mi mathsize="0.710em">K</mi></msubsup></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mpadded style="width:0.481em;" width="0.481em"><mi>J</mi></mpadded><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>𝝉</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\tau}_{t}^{\star}\;=\;\underset{\bm{\tau}\in\{\bm{\tau}^{(k)}_{t}\}_{k=1}^{K}}{\arg\min}\;J\!\left(\bm{\tau}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In contrast to learning-based trajectory ranking <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite> which requires extensive training and often fails under distribution shifts, we propose an explicit, analytic geometric critic.
This module leverages real-time sensor data for robust safety verification without additional supervision.
We discretize each candidate spline <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\tau}^{(k)}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝝉</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\tau}^{(k)}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> into <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> waypoints <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathbf{x}_{j}\}_{j=0}^{M-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathbf{x}_{j}\}_{j=0}^{M-1}</annotation></semantics></math> equidistantly spaced in arc length. The cost <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>J</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J</annotation></semantics></math> of each path is then evaluated using the following terms.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection"><span id="S4.SS4.SSS1.6" class="ltx_text">IV-D</span>1 </span>Discounted Safety Cost</h4>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To score the safety of each trajectory candidate, we build a robot-centric ESDF map <math id="S4.SS4.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E(\mathbf{x})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E(\mathbf{x})</annotation></semantics></math> using the current depth image <math id="S4.SS4.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{D}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐃</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{D}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. Each voxel stores the signed distance to the nearest obstacle surface, where positive values indicate free space and negative values lie inside obstacles.
We prioritize obstacle clearance.
Since the planner operates in a receding-horizon manner and executes only the near-horizon segment before replanning, later waypoints should not be weighted equally. We design a temporal discount factor <math id="S4.SS4.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma\in(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma\in(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math> to prioritize near-field safety:</p>
<table id="S4.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{\text{esdf}}\bigl(\tau_{t}^{(k)}\bigr)=\frac{1}{\sum_{j=0}^{M-1}\gamma^{j}}\sum_{j=0}^{M-1}\gamma^{j}\max\bigl(0,\ d_{\text{safe}}-E(\mathbf{x}^{(k)}_{j})\bigr)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mtext>esdf</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>j</mi></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munderover><mrow><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>j</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>safe</mtext></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>j</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{\text{esdf}}\bigl(\tau_{t}^{(k)}\bigr)=\frac{1}{\sum_{j=0}^{M-1}\gamma^{j}}\sum_{j=0}^{M-1}\gamma^{j}\max\bigl(0,\ d_{\text{safe}}-E(\mathbf{x}^{(k)}_{j})\bigr),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS4.SSS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E(\mathbf{x})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E(\mathbf{x})</annotation></semantics></math> is the ESDF value at position <math id="S4.SS4.SSS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S4.SS4.SSS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\text{safe}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>safe</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\text{safe}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the desired safety margin. This formulation imposes a weighted penalty on clearance violations, placing greater importance on the near-horizon segment of the execution path.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection"><span id="S4.SS4.SSS2.6" class="ltx_text">IV-D</span>2 </span>Path Efficiency</h4>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To encourage the efficiency of the selected plan, we penalize unnecessary detours and prioritize candidates that terminate closest to the local goal <math id="S4.SS4.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{g}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐠</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{g}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
<table id="S4.E7" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="S4.E7X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E7X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle J_{\text{len}}\bigl(\bm{\tau}^{(k)}_{t}\bigr)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mtext>len</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝝉</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle J_{\text{len}}\bigl(\bm{\tau}^{(k)}_{t}\bigr)</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E7Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle J_{\text{goal}}\bigl(\bm{\tau}^{(k)}_{t}\bigr)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mtext>goal</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝝉</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle J_{\text{goal}}\bigl(\bm{\tau}^{(k)}_{t}\bigr)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E7Xa.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\left\|\mathbf{x}^{(k)}_{M-1}-\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\|_{2}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo>‖</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐠</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\left\|\mathbf{x}^{(k)}_{M-1}-\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\|_{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The total trajectory cost for each candidate path is a weighted sum of the three terms:</p>
<table id="S4.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J\bigl(\tau_{t}^{(k)}\bigr)=\lambda_{\text{1}}\,J_{\text{safe}}\bigl(\tau_{t}^{(k)}\bigr)+\lambda_{\text{2}}\,J_{\text{len}}\bigl(\tau_{t}^{(k)}\bigr)+\lambda_{\text{3}}\,J_{\text{goal}}\bigl(\tau_{t}^{(k)}\bigr)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>2</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>J</mi><mtext>len</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>3</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>J</mi><mtext>goal</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J\bigl(\tau_{t}^{(k)}\bigr)=\lambda_{\text{1}}\,J_{\text{safe}}\bigl(\tau_{t}^{(k)}\bigr)+\lambda_{\text{2}}\,J_{\text{len}}\bigl(\tau_{t}^{(k)}\bigr)+\lambda_{\text{3}}\,J_{\text{goal}}\bigl(\tau_{t}^{(k)}\bigr),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS4.SSS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{1}},\lambda_{\text{2}},\lambda_{\text{3}}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>1</mtext></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>2</mtext></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>3</mtext></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{1}},\lambda_{\text{2}},\lambda_{\text{3}}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> balance safety and efficiency.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section conduct experiments to answer these questions:</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S5.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S5.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Q1.</span> How well is SanD-Planner compared to other vision-based baselines? (Section <a href="#S5.SS2" title="V-B Quantitative Performance Comparison ‣ V Experiments ‣ SanD-Planner: Sample-Efficient Diffusion Planner in B-Spline Space for Robust Local Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">V-B</span></a>)</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Q2.</span> How does SanD-Planner scale with the number of expert trajectories (<span id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">i.e.,</span> sample efficiency)? (Section <a href="#S5.SS3" title="V-C Sample Efficiency and Data Scaling ‣ V Experiments ‣ SanD-Planner: Sample-Efficient Diffusion Planner in B-Spline Space for Robust Local Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">V-C</span></a>)</p>

<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S5.SS1.6" class="ltx_text">V-A</span> </span><span id="S5.SS1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Experimental Setup</span></h3>

<section id="S5.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection"><span id="S5.SS1.SSS1.6" class="ltx_text">V-A</span>1 </span>Training Dataset and Implementation Details</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our training dataset is collected entirely in simulation across 10 diverse environments, including two photorealistic Matterport3D scenes <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib53" title="" class="ltx_ref">48</a>]</cite> and eight Gazebo worlds comprising tunnels and indoor layouts <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite>. To facilitate <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>D local planning, we explicitly incorporate multi-level structures (<span id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">e.g.,</span> stairs) and low-clearance obstacles. We collect <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="500" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>500</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">500</annotation></semantics></math> navigation episodes using the PCT-planner <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib52" title="" class="ltx_ref">49</a>]</cite> as the expert to generate collision-free <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>D trajectories while logging the egocentric depth stream.
To maximize data efficiency, we construct training pairs by randomly sampling sub-trajectories from each expert episode. Each segment is defined by a random start pose and a future waypoint along the same expert path, which is then fitted with a clamped cubic B-spline using eight control points.
This resampling strategy generates diverse and informative labels from a limited set of demonstrations, significantly enhancing the policy’s sample efficiency.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The model is trained on a desktop equipped with an NVIDIA RTX<math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4080" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4080</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4080</annotation></semantics></math> GPU, requiring approximately <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> hours to converge on the <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="500" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>500</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">500</annotation></semantics></math>-trajectory dataset. During inference, candidate trajectories are sampled using the deterministic DPM-Solver++ <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">50</a>]</cite>, achieving an operational frequency of approximately <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8Hz" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8Hz</annotation></semantics></math>. For real-world validation in Section <a href="#S5.SS6" title="V-F Real-world Experiments ‣ V Experiments ‣ SanD-Planner: Sample-Efficient Diffusion Planner in B-Spline Space for Robust Local Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">V-F</span></a>, the system is deployed on a laptop with an RTX<math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4090" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4090</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4090</annotation></semantics></math> to ensure low-latency planning during autonomous navigation.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F4" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_3">

</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F4.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Fig. 4</span>: </span><span id="S5.F4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Comparison of depth images. <figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F5.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Fig. 5</span>: </span><span id="S5.F5.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Simulation benchmark environments <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite>. </figure>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS1.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection"><span id="S5.SS1.SSS2.6" class="ltx_text">V-A</span>2 </span>Observation Domain Randomization</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To bridge the sim-to-real gap, we apply domain randomization to observations during training:
<span id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1) Temporal Latency:</span> we introduce a temporal freezing mechanism to mimic compute and communication delays. With a probability of <math id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1</annotation></semantics></math>, we either freeze the observation buffer <math id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> to the latest frame or replicate individual frames from their predecessors, simulating signal loss or cold starts.
<span id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">2) Sensor Noise:</span> We emulate noise patterns characteristic of the Intel RealSense D435. Following parameters in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">51</a>]</cite>, we inject distance-dependent axial noise that scales quadratically with depth, as visualized in Fig. <a href="#S5.F4" title="Fig. 4 ‣ V-A1 Training Dataset and Implementation Details ‣ V-A Experimental Setup ‣ V Experiments ‣ SanD-Planner: Sample-Efficient Diffusion Planner in B-Spline Space for Robust Local Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>. We also synthesize random pixel dropouts (<math id="S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1</annotation></semantics></math> probability), a stereo-occlusion band on the left margin, and spatially correlated speckle noise.
Such perturbations force the policy to prioritize structural geometric cues over perfect depth measurements.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS1.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection"><span id="S5.SS1.SSS3.6" class="ltx_text">V-A</span>3 </span>Simulation Benchmark</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate SanD-Planner using the InternNav Benchmark <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite>, which provides photorealistic indoor environments designed to minimize the sim-to-real gap for local obstacle avoidance. The benchmark features diverse assets and predefined start-goal pairs for point-goal navigation. To ensure a fair comparison, all baselines are evaluated under the same protocol as shown in Fig. <a href="#S5.F5" title="Fig. 5 ‣ V-A1 Training Dataset and Implementation Details ‣ V-A Experimental Setup ‣ V Experiments ‣ SanD-Planner: Sample-Efficient Diffusion Planner in B-Spline Space for Robust Local Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T1" class="ltx_table">

<td id="S5.T1.10.3.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_l ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center" style="padding-top:-0.45pt;padding-bottom:-0.45pt;"><math id="S5.T1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="72.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn mathsize="0.800em">72.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">72.3</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>

</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S5.SS2.6" class="ltx_text">V-B</span> </span><span id="S5.SS2.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Quantitative Performance Comparison</span></h3>

<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate SanD-Planner against three SoTA visual planners: iPlanner <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite>, ViPlanner <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>, and NavDP <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite>, regarding the point-goal navigation task.
Following the benchmark protocol, we report Success Rate (SR) and Success weighted by Path Length (SPL) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">52</a>]</cite> across <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2020" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2020</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2020</annotation></semantics></math> episodes in ClutteredEnv and <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4040" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4040</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4040</annotation></semantics></math> episodes in InternScenes.
Notably, despite training on only <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="500" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>500</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">500</annotation></semantics></math> trajectories (<math id="S5.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\approx\textbf{0.25\%}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≈</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">0.25%</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx\textbf{0.25\%}</annotation></semantics></math> of the <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="200" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>200</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">200</annotation></semantics></math>k trajectories used by NavDP), SanD-Planner achieves competitive or superior performance across both benchmarks (Table <a href="#S5.T1" title="TABLE I ‣ V-A3 Simulation Benchmark ‣ V-A Experimental Setup ‣ V Experiments ‣ SanD-Planner: Sample-Efficient Diffusion Planner in B-Spline Space for Robust Local Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I</span></a>).
On the realistic InternScenes, SanD-Planner outperforms NavDP by large margins (<math id="S5.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+6.3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>6.3</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+6.3\%</annotation></semantics></math> SR and <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.0\%</annotation></semantics></math> SPL), demonstrating robust generalization to complex indoor layouts and diverse obstacle distributions. In ClutteredEnv, SanD-Planner achieves the highest <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="90.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>90.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">90.1\%</annotation></semantics></math> SR while maintaining a competitive <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="84.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>84.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">84.0\%</annotation></semantics></math> SPL. The slight SPL gap compared to NavDP is partly attributable to the B-spline parameterization, which embeds a structural bias toward safer, albeit more conservative, detours. However, analysis in Section <a href="#S5.SS3" title="V-C Sample Efficiency and Data Scaling ‣ V Experiments ‣ SanD-Planner: Sample-Efficient Diffusion Planner in B-Spline Space for Robust Local Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">V-C</span></a> suggests this gap arises from the limited data scale rather than methodological constraints and could be further narrowed with additional supervision.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The performance comparison between iPlanner (depth-only) and ViPlanner (depth and semantics) highlights the trade-offs of multi-modal inputs. While ViPlanner leverages semantics in InternScenes (<math id="S5.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+5.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>5.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+5.5\%</annotation></semantics></math> SR over iPlanner), it suffers a severe performance degradation in ClutteredEnv (<math id="S5.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-12.4\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>12.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-12.4\%</annotation></semantics></math> SR), where primitive obstacles lack well-defined semantic categories. This underscores the potential brittleness of relying on semantic cues under distribution shifts. Crucially, SanD-Planner outperforms ViPlanner on both benchmarks using depth observations alone. These results suggest that depth information provides sufficient geometric cues for general 2D collision avoidance, whereas semantics may degrade model generalization in OOD scenes when training data is limited.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, we distinguish our results from iPlanner and ViPlanner due to their different training paradigms; these methods learn differentiable cost maps from discrete samples (<span id="S5.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">e.g.,</span> <math id="S5.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>30</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30</annotation></semantics></math>k images) rather than continuous expert trajectories.
NavDP, being a full-trajectory IL-based method, serves as the most direct baseline. As detailed in Table <a href="#S5.T2" title="TABLE II ‣ V-A3 Simulation Benchmark ‣ V-A Experimental Setup ‣ V Experiments ‣ SanD-Planner: Sample-Efficient Diffusion Planner in B-Spline Space for Robust Local Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">II</span></a>, SanD-Planner demonstrates superior efficiency, requiring orders of magnitude less training data and compute to achieve SoTA performance.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F6" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.00923v1/Images/Ablation_experiemnt_Bspline_cubic_waypoint.png" id="S5.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/291;" width="476" height="291" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F6.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Fig. 6</span>: </span><span id="S5.F6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Comparison of trajectory representations in simulation. Top-right: the scene reconstruction with the same start and goal. For each representation (discrete waypoints, cubic spline, and B-spline), we show the ego-view image and a bird-view radar visualization with <math id="S5.F6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> candidate trajectories overlaid.</span></figcaption>
</figure>

</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S5.SS3.6" class="ltx_text">V-C</span> </span><span id="S5.SS3.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sample Efficiency and Data Scaling</span></h3>

<div id="S5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We investigate the sample efficiency of SanD-Planner by training on trajectory-level subsets ranging from <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the full dataset.
As shown in Fig. <a href="#S5.F7" title="Fig. 7 ‣ V-D Ablation Study on Trajectory Representation ‣ V Experiments ‣ SanD-Planner: Sample-Efficient Diffusion Planner in B-Spline Space for Robust Local Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>, our approach exhibits monotonic performance gains as the number of demonstrations increases. Notably, the model is highly efficient even in data-scarce regimes, achieving a non-trivial <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="55.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>55.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">55.5\%</annotation></semantics></math> SR with only <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50</annotation></semantics></math> expert trajectories (<math id="S5.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10\%</annotation></semantics></math> data).
With <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="250" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>250</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">250</annotation></semantics></math> trajectories (<math id="S5.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>50</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50\%</annotation></semantics></math> data), the model attains <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="65.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>65.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">65.0\%</annotation></semantics></math> SR, recovering <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="76\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>76</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">76\%</annotation></semantics></math> of its peak performance.
While basic collision avoidance is established with minimal data, the SPL metric continues to improve substantially up to the full dataset scale (<math id="S5.SS3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="49.6\%\rightarrow 78.9\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>49.6</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mn>78.9</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">49.6\%\rightarrow 78.9\%</annotation></semantics></math>). This suggests that while small datasets suffice for learning safe behaviors, larger demonstration scales are essential for the planner to internalize more efficient bypass strategies and minimize unnecessary detours.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S5.SS4.6" class="ltx_text">V-D</span> </span><span id="S5.SS4.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Ablation Study on Trajectory Representation</span></h3>

<div id="S5.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To validate the impact of trajectory parameterization, we ablate the output representation while keeping the rest of the navigation pipeline fixed. All variants predict eight anchor points to maintain identical output dimensionality. The discrete waypoint baseline utilizes a fixed <math id="S5.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.2m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.2m</annotation></semantics></math> spacing, resulting in a <math id="S5.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.4m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.4m</annotation></semantics></math> lookahead. In contrast, both interpolating cubic splines <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite> and our B-spline representation parameterize an extended horizon of approximately <math id="S5.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6m</annotation></semantics></math>.
Tab. <a href="#S5.T3" title="TABLE III ‣ V-B Quantitative Performance Comparison ‣ V Experiments ‣ SanD-Planner: Sample-Efficient Diffusion Planner in B-Spline Space for Robust Local Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">III</span></a> shows that the choice of representation influences performance, with B-splines consistently outperforming the alternatives. In ClutteredEnv (episodes <math id="S5.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;20m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;20m</annotation></semantics></math>), discrete waypoints suffer from the myopic behavior <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>]</cite>; while they match cubic splines with <math id="S5.SS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\approx 75\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mn>75</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 75\%</annotation></semantics></math> SR, they exhibit lower efficiency (<math id="S5.SS4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="65.8\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>65.8</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">65.8\%</annotation></semantics></math> vs. <math id="S5.SS4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="70.6\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>70.6</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">70.6\%</annotation></semantics></math> SPL) due to suboptimal detours. Spline-based parameterizations mitigate this by enforcing smoothness and extending the planning horizon within the same parameter budget.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The performance gap of B-splines highlights the critical role of local support. The interpolated cubic splines are globally coupled, causing prediction errors in occluded far-field regions to propagate backward and destabilize the immediate execution segment. Conversely, B-splines possess compact support, which effectively isolates far-field uncertainty and ensures near-field stability. In the confined InternScenesenvironment, the advantage of long-horizon planning is less pronounced due to heavy occlusions. This explains why myopic waypoints slightly outperform cubic splines in such settings. However, B-splines maintain the best overall performance, balancing near-horizon robustness with path efficiency.
Qualitative results in Fig. <a href="#S5.F6" title="Fig. 6 ‣ V-B Quantitative Performance Comparison ‣ V Experiments ‣ SanD-Planner: Sample-Efficient Diffusion Planner in B-Spline Space for Robust Local Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> further illustrate this robustness: waypoints yield non-smooth, less trackable paths, and cubic splines amplify prediction noise across the entire curve. In contrast, B-splines generate consistent candidates with localized variations, demonstrating lower sensitivity to perceptual uncertainty.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F7" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.00923v1/Images/efficiency.png" id="S5.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:405/228;" width="405" height="228" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F7.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Fig. 7</span>: </span><span id="S5.F7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Ablation study on training data size in ClutterEnv. SR and SPL improve consistently with training dataset size.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S5.T4" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:80%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S5.T4.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:113%;">TABLE IV</span>: </span><span id="S5.T4.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:113%;">Velocity-token ablation on ClutteredEnv scenes.</span></figcaption>

<tr id="S5.T4.7.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S5.T4.7.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_border_tt" style="padding-top:-0.45pt;padding-bottom:-0.45pt;"></td>

<td id="S5.T4.7.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_l ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt" style="padding-top:-0.45pt;padding-bottom:-0.45pt;" colspan="2"><span id="S5.T4.7.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;">w/ token</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S5.T4.7.2" class="ltx_tr">

<td id="S5.T4.7.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_l ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:-0.45pt;padding-bottom:-0.45pt;"><span id="S5.T4.7.2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;">SR<span id="S5.T4.7.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> [%]<math id="S5.T4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\uparrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↑</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\uparrow</annotation></semantics></math></span></span></td>

</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="S5.F8.fig2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2602.00923v1/Images/reconstruction_2.png" id="S5.F8.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_portrait" style="aspect-ratio:476/879;" width="476" height="879" alt="Refer to caption">
</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F8.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Fig. 8</span>: </span><span id="S5.F8.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Representative comparison of trajectory consistency with and without the velocity token.<span id="S5.F8.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> We visualize the diffusion-sampled bypass candidates (blue) at each planning step <math id="S5.F8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>. Without the velocity token (top), the candidate set remains highly multi-modal and dispersed, and the critic-selected solution alternates between bypass modes across consecutive replans, producing inconsistent heading directions (arrows) and eventually leading to a collision. With the velocity token (bottom), the sampled candidates are more temporally consistent, yielding stable headings and a safe bypass.
The rightmost panel shows the corresponding 3D reconstructions from Depth Anything 3 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">53</a>]</cite>, where the cyan curve indicates the camera/robot trajectory.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S5.SS5.6" class="ltx_text">V-E</span> </span><span id="S5.SS5.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Ablation Study on Velocity Token for Temporal Consistency</span></h3>

<div id="S5.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate the impact of previous plan information on planning consistency by ablating the velocity token <math id="S5.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{t}^{\mathrm{prev}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>prev</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{t}^{\mathrm{prev}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
As reported in Table <a href="#S5.T4" title="TABLE IV ‣ V-D Ablation Study on Trajectory Representation ‣ V Experiments ‣ SanD-Planner: Sample-Efficient Diffusion Planner in B-Spline Space for Robust Local Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">IV</span></a>, removing this temporal conditioning leads to a consistent performance drop, which confirms its necessity for trajectory reliability.
Analysis reveals that collisions without <math id="S5.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{t}^{\mathrm{prev}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>prev</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{t}^{\mathrm{prev}}</annotation></semantics></math> frequently occur near geometrically symmetric obstacles (<span id="S5.SS5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">e.g.,</span> pillars), where an example is shown in Fig. <a href="#S5.F8" title="Fig. 8 ‣ V-D Ablation Study on Trajectory Representation ‣ V Experiments ‣ SanD-Planner: Sample-Efficient Diffusion Planner in B-Spline Space for Robust Local Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>.
Under partial observability, such structures induce bimodal distributions of plausible bypass trajectories. Without velocity conditioning, the diffusion model generates dispersed, high-variance candidates at each step.
Since the critic selects the optimal trajectory independently per step, the planner suffers from topological inconsistency, frequently switching between conflicting bypass modes. This results in oscillatory steering and eventual collisions.
In contrast, the <math id="S5.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{t}^{\mathrm{prev}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>prev</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{t}^{\mathrm{prev}}</annotation></semantics></math> condition effectively regularizes the generative process, yielding concentrated candidate sets consistent with the robot’s established motion and ensuring a stable heading.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S5.SS6.6" class="ltx_text">V-F</span> </span><span id="S5.SS6.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Real-world Experiments</span></h3>

<div id="S5.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Real-world experiments are deployed on a Unitree Go2 quadruped robot. The platform features an Intel RealSense D<math id="S5.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="435" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>435</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">435</annotation></semantics></math> depth camera with an IR-pass filter, with algorithms executed on a tethered laptop.
We evaluate the system’s zero-shot sim-to-real capability without any fine-tuning or domain adaptation.
The planner operates at approximately <math id="S5.SS6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10Hz" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10Hz</annotation></semantics></math>, with trajectories tracked by an onboard MPC controller <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite>. To facilitate high-frequency replanning in a receding-horizon setting, we employ a warm-start strategy: subsequent planning cycles initialize from the previous solution and undergo partial denoising (starting from step <math id="S5.SS6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S5.SS6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math>). At each step, <math id="S5.SS6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=16</annotation></semantics></math> candidate trajectories are sampled in parallel, with the optimal plan selected by the geometric critic module.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To assess SanD-Planner’s zero-shot generalization, we conduct experiments across diverse scenarios with static and dynamic pedestrians, as shown in Fig. <a href="#S0.F1" title="Fig. 1 ‣ SanD-Planner: Sample-Efficient Diffusion Planner in B-Spline Space for Robust Local Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> and Fig. <a href="#S5.F9" title="Fig. 9 ‣ V-F Real-world Experiments ‣ V Experiments ‣ SanD-Planner: Sample-Efficient Diffusion Planner in B-Spline Space for Robust Local Navigation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>.
Static tests include narrow mazes and cluttered office environments with tight clearances. We further evaluate outdoor navigation, where illumination changes and complex geometries present significantly more challenging perception conditions than simulation. Additionally, we demonstrate <math id="S5.SS6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>D navigation capability through stair-climbing trials. Despite these challenges, SanD-Planner generates smooth, collision-avoiding trajectories, confirming the effectiveness and zero-shot capability of our method.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F9" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.00923v1/Images/real_figure.png" id="S5.F9.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:438/246;" width="438" height="246" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F9.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Fig. 9</span>: </span><span id="S5.F9.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Demonstrations of SanD-Planner in unseen environments. Depth inputs and predicted trajectories are also shown, with the selected trajectory is hightlight in green.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">VI </span><span id="S6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Conclusion and Future Work</span></h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This paper presents SanD-Planner, a sample-efficient, diffusion-based planner using clamped cubic B-spline parameterization.
By predicting control points and decoupling the safety check via a critic module, our method reduces learning complexity and data dependency.
Benchmarks show that with only <math id="S6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="500" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>500</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">500</annotation></semantics></math> expert episodes, SanD-Planner matches or surpasses SoTA performance.
Our findings suggest that:
1) B-splines isolate sensing uncertainty better than waypoints or interpolating splines, yielding more stable planning; and 2) depth sensing provides sufficient geometric cues for collision avoidance.
Zero-shot real-world deployment further validates our method, enabling <math id="S6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>D and <math id="S6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>D navigation tasks such as point-goal navigation and stair traversal without any fine-tuning.
Despite its competitive performance, SanD-Planner is limited by depth sensors regarding small
or specular objects.
Future work will explore integrating visual foundation models to achieve more robust metric depth estimation and environmental resilience. And even though our primary focus is on sample efficiency, the data scaling experiments reveal the model’s untapped potential. We will also plan to leverage this scalability to train on larger, more diverse datasets, aiming to extend the system’s generalization across varied environments.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>

      all.</p>
    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
  </div>
